title: Constructing the compatible module direct image from geometric ring data
statement: Let (C,J),(D,K) be small sites and A,B commutative ring sheaves. Every geometric ring datum g for A and B has a compatible induced module direct image: an additive functor Mod(A)→Mod(B), an underlying-sheaf natural isomorphism to g.direct, and the generalized-element scalar-action and addition identity under g.adj, exactly as required by RingedToposMorphism.

source.place: Pushforward of modules, Lemma lemma-pushforward-module (03D1), and ringed-topos definition; construction expanded as operations on the specified direct-image sheaf.

proof.text: Let d be the adjunct B→V(A) of the structural ring map. Express its generalized-element addition, multiplication and unit identities as maps from the binary product and terminal sheaves. The product Hom-adjunction identities make d a ring map for the transported operations.

Use the existing concrete imageFunctor construction with V, d and these identities. Its underlying sheaf is literally V(M), with addition transported by V and scalar action restricted along d. The existing image-module construction proves the module laws and linear restrictions and obtains sheafhood from V(M). On morphisms it applies V. The underlying comparison is the identity.

For additivity, write the underlying map of f+h as pairing the underlying maps of f and h followed by addition. V preserves this pairing by the inverse product comparison, which is exactly the addition of the image module.

Write z=a*x+y as the composite of the action and addition operation maps. Rewrite them by the constructed transported operations. The counit pair and binary-operation identities send this expression to the original action and addition, and the triangle identity identifies the adjunct of a;d with L(a);g.ringMap. Evaluation on sections is module_linear.

proof_origin.place: Explicit Lean construction and operation calculations, expanding the transport details omitted in Tag 03CR.

mathlib_searches.query: A geometric morphism of sheaf topoi and a ring object morphism induces a functor on sheaves of modules
mathlib_searches.verdict: Only scheme and continuous-site specializations were returned. Used the existing library finite-product and sectionwise constructions instead.

mathlib_searches.verdict: Use these projection identities to prove the new compatibility lemmas; no exact interface already exists.
